data.long_meaning: In Aramaic, Bartolome means 'son of Talmai'. In Greek, it is derived from the name Bartholomaios, which means 'son of Talmai' or 'son of the furrow'. Bartolome is mentioned in the New Testament as one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.

data.cultural_impact: Bartolome is a name of reverence and respect within the Christian community, particularly in Spain and Portugal. Saint Bartholomew is one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus, who is believed to have preached the Gospel in various regions of the Middle East, Armenia, and even India. The feast day of Saint Bartholomew, August 24, is celebrated with much fervor, particularly in the Iberian Peninsula. The cult of Saint Bartholomew has also produced numerous works of art and literature, further cementing his place in Western spiritual and cultural history.
data.spiritual_significance: Bartolome represents the enduring power and spread of the Christian faith. As an apostle, he played a role in the spreading of the Good News of Jesus Christ. In his name, we are reminded of the importance of being a messenger of faith and living our lives in accordance with God's will. Moreover, the name Bartolome bring to mind the suffering and martyrdom of Saint Bartholomew, who is believed to have been flayed alive. Thus, the name represents a call to bear witness to our beliefs, even in the face of adversity and persecution.
